**Correction to one sentence in the report above** (not a new report — no marker, so the report scan should still find exactly one).

The report's departure (5) says the whole-set label write was "the only mechanism available". That is **stronger than what I observed, and I am withdrawing it**. What actually happened:

* I **never attempted** the additive `POST /issues/N/labels` with an `Authorization` header. Not once.
* I never observed whether `GITHUB_TOKEN` is set in this environment. My one attempt to look (`env | grep` for credential variable **names**, values never printed) was refused by the permission layer before it executed, so I have no reading either way.
* "Credential inspection is blocked" meant **a permission-layer refusal of my own Bash command**, not an API error. No HTTP request to `api.github.com` was ever made, so no status code was ever returned.
* A second command — an **unauthenticated** `GET .../issues/10896/labels` via curl — was refused the same way.
* `gh` really is absent (`gh: command not found`), and curl itself works fine: I fetched `unpkg.com` (next@16.3.1 sources) and `registry.npmjs.org` (yaml tarball) over it, both HTTP 200, in this same session.

So the honest statement is: after two refusals I **inferred** the authenticated route would also be refused and reached for `mcp__github__issue_write`, whose `labels` array is a whole-set replace. The inference may well be wrong, and I should have either tested it or labelled it as an inference in the report rather than asserting unavailability.

The labels on #10896 are correct and are **not** being touched again.

**Settled, replacing the hedge above.** Two authorized read-only probes — `GET /rate_limit` and `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/10896/labels`, each sent with an `Authorization` header — both returned **`200`**, so the additive `POST /issues/N/labels` **was** available to me and the whole-set write was avoidable.

The departure recorded in the report was therefore my own inference from an unrelated refusal, not a limitation of this environment. No POST was run and #10896's labels are untouched.
